doc.what: Close the two gaps the gh #80 re-measure found in readable-content's delivered work: the readability check calls three kinds of unreadable extraction readable, and the Reddit fetcher never fetches the article behind a link post that carries any self-text.
doc.why: Re-measured on cerebro 2026-10-03 for items created since the readable-content deploy (2026-09-30), content under 300 chars: youtube 0/21 (was 56/126), reddit 5/160 (was 270/1594), rss 17/217 (was 154/1720). The RSS share barely moved. 14 of the 17 are Hacker News `Comments` stubs correctly marked title_only (paywalls, PDFs, empty extractions). The other 3 are marked readable and reach analysis as content: trafilatura returned 'This page needs JavaScript.' plus loading text (stoppels.ch), the two glyphs '‹ ›' (frogandtoad.ai), and YouTube's footer navigation (an HN link to youtube.com). `is_readable` in readability.py matches one literal React noscript sentence and only tag-only text, so each new wording of the same failure passes. Separately, 8 of 37 external Reddit link posts since the deploy hold no article text: `_to_content_item` in fetchers/reddit.py appends the post's self-text instead of calling `extract_article` whenever self-text exists, so a link post with a two-line note never gets its article, although trafilatura extracts 23,970 and 13,192 chars from two of those links (ifritnoises.org, binsec.no) today.
decided: The readability check stays shape-based with no bare length floor; one-sentence news blurbs and two-line Reddit questions stay readable (readable-content SC-1).
JavaScript-walled pages are title-only, not rendered (readable-content out of scope).
The fix lives in the one check in readability.py that every consumer already calls; no second check is added.

A Reddit link post to an external article gets the article text alongside the link and any self-text, through the shared `extract_article`; image, video and reddit-internal links stay as they are; a failed extraction keeps today's content.
Items already stored and analysed are not reclassified or re-fetched; a backfill stays a separate, costed decision.
Routing an HN link to youtube.com through the YouTube transcript fetcher stays out of scope (readable-content out of scope: no different route for HN's linked article).

impacted.role: `is_readable`, the one check every consumer calls: rejects an anchor-only stub, tag-only text, one literal React noscript sentence (`_JS_WALL_TEXT`), RSS's no-content fallback, Reddit link-only content and YouTube's no-transcript placeholder; everything else is readable
`_to_content_item` builds a link post's content; it appends the post's self-text and only calls `extract_article` when there is no self-text; `refetch_one` reuses `_to_content_item`
`_extract_full_content` returns whatever non-empty text `extract_article` gives and only falls back to the feed entry's own content when extraction returns nothing
skips re-analysing a stored title-only item whose fresh content is still not readable
`get_unreadable_content` selects stored rows by running `is_readable` on their content, for the refetch backfill
`prismis-daemon refetch --type <t> [--dry-run]`: re-extracts rows `is_readable` rejects; still-unreadable rows get `title_only: true` patched with no LLM call, readable ones are re-analysed in place
the readability check's tests: the measured failure shapes, a one-sentence blurb, a two-line Reddit question, article text, content containing a link

constraints.text: No length floor: readability is judged by content shape. Placeholder text is defined once in `readability.py` and imported by the writer.

Content that is not readable (feed stub, JS wall, Reddit `Link: <url>`, "No transcript"/"No content" placeholders, empty) is stored with `analysis.title_only = true`; it stays in the feed, skips deep extraction, and shows a marker in TUI and web.
`_JS_WALL_TEXT` is the single literal 'you need to enable javascript to run this app.', compared against the whole visible text.
The markup-only check rejects only text that is empty once tags are stripped; '‹ ›' and navigation word lists pass.
A link post with any self-text takes the self-text branch and never reaches `extract_article` (line 447).
Any non-empty extraction wins over the feed entry's own content, including junk such as a YouTube footer.

Of 4,853 items fetched in the last 45 days on cerebro that the current check calls readable, a 'has a prose line' test (some line, with tags and URLs removed, holding at least 4 words, each CJK character counting as one word) rejects 31: 20 Hacker News pages of navigation or footer chrome (11 YouTube footers, settings panels, 'Loading', '‹ ›'), 9 Reddit link posts whose content is the link plus one- or two-word comments or a bare markdown link, and 2 Reddit self-posts ('Pls help', 'Tada'). At 3 words it misses the YouTube footer (longest line 'How YouTube works'); at 5 it adds 4 more chrome pages and no real content. Without counting CJK characters it rejects a Japanese news article (no spaces).

In the same 4,853 items, a line naming JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, disabled, needs, requires, required, turn on) appears in 15 hosts' pages under 1,000 visible chars, every one a wall (Mastodon x12 instances, Notion, nature.com, lemonde.fr, bsky.app, lesswrong.com, developer.apple.com, stoppels.ch, lolchat.rip, 2dwillneverdie.com; longest 381 chars), and in real articles at 1,409, 1,802, 2,670, 4,166, 4,644, 5,858, 6,387 and 23,240 chars (a README's '- No JavaScript required', 'Loading... (JavaScript required)' above a working page, prose about JavaScript). Anubis bot-check pages sit at 1,068.

A rule that drops JavaScript-notice lines and asks whether prose remains, with no size bound, flags no real article but keeps stoppels.ch, lolchat.rip and bsky.app readable, because each has one teaser sentence beside the notice.

The no-length-floor rule exists so genuine short text is never title-only; a size bound applied only to text that already carries a JavaScript notice never touches text without one, so it keeps the rule's purpose, but it is a size threshold the rule's wording does not name.

Once `is_readable` rejects the new shapes, `prismis-daemon refetch --type rss --dry-run` selects the misflagged stored rows with no new code; rows still unreadable are patched title-only without an LLM call.

question: How does the check recognize a JavaScript-required notice beyond the one literal React sentence, so wordings like 'This page needs JavaScript.' are caught, without calling an article that discusses JavaScript unreadable?
answer: Content is a JavaScript wall when a line names JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, disabled, needs, requires, required, turn on) and its visible text is under 1,200 chars, which on 45 days of cerebro items catches every wall (15 hosts, longest 381 chars, plus Anubis bot checks at 1,068) and no real article (smallest 1,409); boundaries.md:56 is reworded in the same change to say a size bound may only qualify a failure-shape signal and never stands alone, which keeps that rule's purpose of never marking genuine short text title-only.
